name: MCP Resource-bound Authorization
mechanism: Validates issuer, audience, resource, scope and user delegation for each protected remote MCP request and obtains separate credentials for downstream APIs instead of forwarding inbound tokens.
use_when: Remote MCP servers expose user-specific or sensitive operations
MCP proxies call protected downstream APIs
avoid_when: A local stdio server has no remote authorization surface
The server accepts generic bearer audiences or uses sessions as authentication
expected_effects: Auditable user and resource binding for MCP operations
failure_modes: Inbound tokens are passed to upstream APIs
Generic audience tokens work across servers
Session identifiers substitute for authenticated identity
